title: Initialization Request Contract
purpose: Defines the atomic JSON initialization request for the bounded local initialization workflow.

normative_requirements.text: An initialization request shall be one JSON object that explicitly supplies a governing authority identity, a product identifier, an absent destination path, a local source repository path, an exact source revision identifier, and product-direction material.

The governing authority identity, product identifier, destination path, local source repository path, exact source revision identifier, and product-direction material shall be required; the request shall be rejected when any required field is missing, empty, or structurally invalid.
The initialization request representation shall be JSON and shall not infer omitted authority-bearing values from environment state, repository configuration, remote services, or named references.

The request root object shall define exactly the following fields: required `schema_version` as a string, required `destination` as a string, required `authority` as an object, required `source` as an object, required `product` as an object, and optional `profile` as a string; the request shall be rejected when any other root field is present.

The `authority` object shall define required `granted_by` as a non-empty opaque string identifying the governing request authority, optional `type` as a non-empty string naming the authority type (such as `governing-issue`, `review-proposal`, or `local-bootstrap`), and optional `scope` as a non-empty string, and shall be rejected when any other authority field is present.

The `source` object shall define required `repository` as a non-empty string naming the local source repository path and required `revision` as an object conforming to the canonical Git object identity representation defined by product.git-object-identity with object_format "sha1", and shall be rejected when any other source field is present.

The `product` object shall define required `id` as a non-empty string product identifier conforming to the product-identity contract and required `direction_material` as a non-empty array of non-empty strings, and shall be rejected when any other product field is present.

The `direction_material` array shall contain at least one item, shall preserve the supplied order of items, shall preserve duplicate items exactly as supplied without deduplication or reordering, and each item shall be a non-empty repository-relative path within the local source repository that names supplied product-direction material; duplicate source entries shall each receive their own distinct positional index and each occurrence shall produce its own deterministic evidence path, and duplicates shall not be deduplicated, collapsed, or merged.

At intake, each `direction_material` entry shall be validated as a non-empty repository-relative path without reading source content. During source-material resolution, before the request is accepted for destination preflight or staging, each entry shall be validated against the specified source revision and shall resolve to an existing regular file. The request shall be rejected and its intake-produced fingerprint shall not authorize destination preflight, staging, or later success-path processing when any direction_material entry resolves to a nonexistent path, a directory, a symbolic link, a path outside the source repository, or a non-regular file; use of the fingerprint solely to identify a governed failure diagnostic remains controlled by the applicable lifecycle and record specifications.

Content from each `direction_material` entry shall be copied verbatim from the source repository into the staging workspace during foundation seeding; duplicate entries shall each contribute their content independently. Each direction_material entry is assigned a positional 0-based array index, and evidence paths follow the pattern product/docs/direction/evidence/{index:03d}-{basename} as defined by the output inventory (product.initializer-output-inventory-v1).

The `destination` path and `source.repository` path shall be interpreted as Version 1 local filesystem paths using `/` as the sole separator and an invoking process working directory that is an absolute path beginning with `/`; an invocation whose working directory cannot be represented by this syntax is unsupported and shall be rejected. At intake, normalization shall operate on strings without using a host path-normalization library: for a relative supplied path, prepend the working-directory segments; for an absolute supplied path, begin at the root; split on `/`; discard empty and `.` segments; for each `..` segment remove the preceding retained segment when one exists and otherwise remain at the root; retain every other segment Unicode scalar value for Unicode scalar value; and return `/` followed by the retained segments joined by single `/` separators, or `/` when none remain. Thus multiple leading separators, including `//`, normalize to one root separator. Reverse solidus and colon have no separator or drive-prefix meaning under this grammar and remain ordinary segment characters unless another request rule rejects the value. The path strings shall not contain U+0000. Tilde expansion, environment-variable expansion, filesystem canonicalization, and symbolic-link resolution shall not occur. These resolved absolute path strings shall replace the supplied path strings in the validated request model and shall be the path values used by the canonical request representation and every downstream consumer. Path resolution shall be the only accepted-value transformation; the request shall be rejected when a path names a URL, a named reference, or a remote identity.

The `profile` field, when present, shall have the constant value `standard`; the request shall be rejected for any other profile value or profile shape, and `schema_version` shall be the constant string `1` with requests declaring any other schema version rejected.

Request validation shall reject unknown fields at the root and at every nested object, shall reject empty or whitespace-only authority-bearing strings without trimming or normalizing supplied values, and shall reject any string that is not a sequence of Unicode scalar values, including any unpaired UTF-16 surrogate code point represented by a JSON escape. Every accepted value shall be retained verbatim except that `destination` and `source.repository` shall be replaced only by the resolved absolute path strings required by INIT-REQ-009.

The canonical request schema for `schema_version` `1` shall be the representation defined by this specification, and consumers shall not extend, relax, or substitute an alternative schema for the bounded local workflow. After successful intake-local structural and semantic validation and the path resolution required by INIT-REQ-009, the canonical initialization request shall contain the validated fields in this exact order: root `schema_version`, `destination`, `authority`, `source`, `product`, then `profile` when supplied; authority `granted_by`, then `type` and `scope` when supplied; source `repository`, then `revision`; revision `object_format`, then `object_id`; product `id`, then `direction_material`. Source-dependent acceptance under INIT-REQ-015 remains mandatory after intake and shall not alter the canonical representation. An absent optional field shall be omitted and shall not be represented by null, an empty value, or an inferred default. Array order and duplicate occurrences shall be preserved. Except for the two resolved path values, every accepted string value shall be the exact Unicode scalar-value sequence supplied by the request. The canonical JSON byte sequence shall encode that ordered representation as UTF-8 without a byte-order mark; shall use `,` and `:` with no surrounding whitespace; shall use no indentation or other insignificant whitespace; shall encode a quotation mark as bytes `0x5c 0x22`, a reverse solidus as bytes `0x5c 0x5c`, and each control character U+0000 through U+001F as bytes `0x5c 0x75` followed by the four lowercase ASCII hexadecimal digits of its code point; shall emit every other Unicode scalar value directly as UTF-8 without escape encoding; and shall have no terminal newline or other trailing bytes. The request fingerprint shall be the SHA-256 digest of exactly that byte sequence, represented as exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Normative test vector: with invoking working directory `/work`, supplied destination `./output`, supplied source repository `source/../source`, authority `granted_by` value `issue-274`, omitted authority `type`, authority `scope` containing in order the characters `quote`, quotation mark, space, `slash`, reverse solidus, space, `newline`, line feed, space, `snowman`, space, and U+2603, source revision object format `sha1` and object ID `0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567`, product ID `sample-product`, duplicate direction-material values `docs/OVERVIEW.md`, and omitted profile, the canonical byte sequence is the base64 decoding of `` with no additional bytes, and the required request fingerprint is `5bdf14415989c343b3220d7c016b2001843ae27ec675e2640184e33c82540ffe`.

The governing authority identity supplied as `authority.granted_by` shall be the single source of the governing request identifier for the bounded local workflow, shall be passed unchanged to provenance recording, and shall be recorded as the `request_identifier` of the provenance record so every generated authority artifact in the promoted repository traces to the governing request.

The request shall not accept, infer, or substitute any other authority identity and shall be rejected when `authority.granted_by` is absent or empty; consistency of `authority.granted_by` with the provenance record request identifier or with the governing issue linkage shall be validated by repository validation as a pre-promotion check, not by request intake.
